solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Jack comically hosts club contest

indicators.note: to host is to have something inside, so the comedian's name holds the club within it

parts.note: Jack Dee is a British stand-up comedian, so the comic Jack gives his surname
a cricket or baseball bat is a club

explanation.surface: A comedian named Jack presents some sort of club competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack comically' is not an adjective on a name but the comedian Jack Dee; 'hosts' puts BAT inside his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument between opposing sides is a contest of views, a synonym in the noun sense.

clue.text: Mediterranean food Jill latterly produced during parties

indicators.note: during means within, so the letters go inside the parties

parts.note: dos are parties, social functions

indicators.note: latterly points to the end, so only the last letter of Jill is used

parts.note: made means produced

explanation.surface: Jill brought along some Mediterranean nibbles to the parties she went to.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffed vine leaves, a Greek and Turkish dish, are an example of Mediterranean food.

clue.text: Last of patients enters chest surgery — one waits here to get wheeled away

definitions.text: one waits here to get wheeled away

indicators.note: enters means going in, so the final letter goes inside the word for chest

parts.note: a bust is the chest, especially a woman's

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of patients

parts.note: op is short for operation, a surgery

explanation.surface: A patient having chest surgery waits to be wheeled out of the operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hospital trolley; the definition is a place where passengers wait for a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger waits at a stop to be carried off on a wheeled vehicle, a witty roundabout description.

clue.text: Bohemian composer needed in posh magazine? No thanks

indicators.note: needed in places the composer within the shortened magazine title
no here means without, so the thank-you letters are dropped from the title

parts.note: Tatler is an upmarket British society magazine
ta is British slang for thank you
Maurice Ravel was a French composer, of Bolero fame

explanation.surface: A Czech composer is wanted for a society magazine feature, but turns it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bohemian' looks Czech, like Dvorak, but means a nomad. 'No thanks' removes TA from TATLER, leaving TLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian lives an unconventional, wandering life, and a traveller is someone with a roving lifestyle.

clue.text: Duke's found immersed in ale, drunk — one advises Queen

indicators.note: something immersed in a liquid sits inside it, so the duke's letter goes into the mixed-up ale
drunk means the letters of ale are tipsy, knocked out of order

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for duke; the 's is read as 'is'
an aide is an assistant who gives advice

explanation.surface: A duke sits sozzled in the pub while a royal counsellor whispers to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges ALE to AEL and 'immersed in' drops D into it, giving ADEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide was the consort of King William IV, a British queen after whom the Australian city is named.

clue.text: Perhaps something for elevenses — Spanish red? Asti? Doubtful

indicators.note: doubtful suggests the words are uncertain and unsettled, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Spanish red or Asti is a sensible mid-morning drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack, usually tea or coffee and a bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet flaky Danish-style cakes are a typical mid-morning snack, an example of what one might eat at elevenses.

clue.text: Lycra-clad athlete regularly juggled sticks in both hands

indicators.note: sticks in means fixed between, so the picked letters go inside the two hand letters

parts.note: L and R are left and right, both hands

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of juggled

explanation.surface: An athlete in Lycra juggles batons in both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'juggled', UGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobogganer who slides feet first on a sled in a skin-tight suit is a Lycra-clad athlete.

clue.text: One performing in band for a pressing engagement?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in places the performing word inside the band

parts.note: a ring is a circular band
on means performing, as an act on stage

explanation.surface: A musician playing in a band has an urgent gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pressing engagement' sounds urgent but means the task of pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoothing clothes with a hot iron is literally a job of pressing, so it is a pressing engagement.

clue.text: I noisily hired out some of shoes

indicators.note: noisily says the word is to be heard rather than read, giving the organ of sight

parts.note: the pronoun I is said like the organ of sight
let means rented out, as a flat is let

explanation.surface: Someone loudly announces they rented out some of their shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reinforced hole for a lace is a part of a shoe, and shoes have several of them.

clue.text: A stab? Drop of arsenic? Gunfire? It's not informed

indicators.note: a drop of is a tiny amount, so just the first letter of arsenic

parts.note: a shot is a single discharge of gunfire
to be in the dark is to be uninformed

explanation.surface: A murder mystery: stabbing, poisoning or shooting, and no one knows which.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A stab' looks like a knife wound but means a guess, as in 'have a stab at it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to make a guess, and a wild guess is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Funny man turned over lots of money through exercise

indicators.note: one thing running through another is set within it, so the money goes into the exercise

parts.note: a lesson is a piece of schoolwork or practice, an exercise

indicators.note: turned over means the word for the cash is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: a wad is a thick bundle of banknotes

explanation.surface: A comic flipped a fortune by working out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses the cash so it reads DAW. Les Dawson was a much-loved British TV comedian famed for deadpan jokes and deliberately bad piano playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Dawson was a well-known British comedian, so he is an example of a funny man.

clue.text: Round body shy to participate in, say, somersaults

indicators.note: joining in means getting inside the group, so the throw goes inside the reversed abbreviation
a somersault turns head over heels, so the letters for 'say' are read backwards

parts.note: e.g. (exempli gratia) means 'for example', which is 'say'
to shy is to throw, and a lob is a high throw

explanation.surface: A rounded figure is too bashful to join in the acrobatics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like 'bashful' but means a throw; 'somersaults' turns the abbreviation for 'say' backwards so it reads GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere such as the Earth is a round body, and the word also names a model of the planet.

clue.text: Trade's affected by business design style

indicators.note: affected means the letters of trade are acted upon and altered into a new order

parts.note: the word trade as fodder; the 's reads as 'is'
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: Commerce is influenced by a company's look and design ethos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges the trade letters to ARTDE; 'by' is only a link meaning 'next to'.
explanation.definitionFit: The geometric, streamlined decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s is a famous movement in design.

clue.text: Fish and fries nouvelle — chef's latest one to rip off

indicators.note: nouvelle, French for new, as in nouvelle cuisine, signals the letters made anew
one to rip off says a letter is to be torn away from the pool of letters
the latest of a word is its final letter, here the end of chef

explanation.surface: A posh restaurant menu offers fish with new-style chips, the chef ripping off the customers.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AND FRIES, remove F (the last letter of chef, the one 'to rip off'), and 'nouvelle' rearranges the leftover ANDRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily fish of the herring family, often canned, is a common example of a fish.

clue.text: Windows type, in shelter, revolutionary wants to boot out

indicators.note: in places the Windows version inside the reversed shelter
a revolution turns things round, so the word for shelter is read backwards

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
XP is a version of the Microsoft Windows operating system

explanation.surface: A rebel camping out wants to kick out a particular version of Windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a person but reverses LEE into EEL, with XP placed 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone is to force them out, the same as to boot out, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Philosophical dog needing to pee causes complaint?

parts.note: a dog turning philosopher, in the style of Descartes' 'I think, therefore I am', reasons 'I'm (a) pet'
the dog's conclusion, 'therefore I go', is what a dog says when it needs to pee

explanation.surface: A dog with a full bladder reasons like a philosopher, which leads to a medical complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: A canine cogito: 'I'm pet, (therefore) I go'. Read the dog's reasoning as I'M PET I GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagious bacterial skin infection is a complaint in the medical sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Footballer a bit old to play around DIY store with bearings

indicators.note: around means the word for play goes round the shop and the bearings

parts.note: to toy is to play, to fiddle with
MFI was a British chain of flat-pack furniture and DIY stores
NNE is north-north-east, a compass bearing made of three directions

explanation.surface: An ageing footballer fiddles about in a DIY store with ball bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Finney was an English winger of the 1940s and 1950s who played his whole career for Preston North End, so 'a bit old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Tom Finney was an English international footballer of the 1950s, a player from a past era.

clue.text: Game TV presenter wears ornamental fabric

indicators.note: one who wears something has it around them, so the presenter goes inside the fabric

parts.note: lace is a fine decorative openwork fabric
Jonathan Ross is a British television presenter

explanation.surface: A TV presenter dons a frilly fabric for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport played with netted sticks, originating in North America, is a game.

clue.text: Greek premier to count cost during appeal for help

indicators.note: during means within, so the letters go inside the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the first letter of count is used

parts.note: a rate is a price or charge, a cost

explanation.surface: A Greek prime minister reckons up the bill while pleading for a bailout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premier' looks like a prime minister but takes only the first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian philosopher who taught Plato is the most famous Greek thinker, an example of a Greek.

clue.text: Huge female model admits one chemical process

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, huge

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the numeral goes inside the model's name

parts.note: Kate Moss is a famous British fashion model
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A very large model owns up to a single chemistry experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the setter's own pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The passage of a solvent through a membrane from weaker to stronger solution is a chemical or physical process.

clue.text: In record company, Mike replaces Director, creating a spiritual focus

indicators.note: replaces signals one letter swapped for another in the label's name

parts.note: Decca is a British record label
Mike is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for the letter M

explanation.surface: At a record label, a man called Mike ousts the boss and finds religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' is not a person but the radio code word for M, which takes the place of D.
explanation.definitionFit: The holiest city of Islam, a place of pilgrimage, is a spiritual focus, and the word is used for any centre of attraction.

clue.text: Main relative poured out wine

indicators.note: words poured out are spoken in a flow, so the clue is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: key means main, principal, as in a key point; an auntie is a relative

explanation.surface: A close relative tipped out a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poured out' looks like what happens to wine but here means spoken; KEY plus AUNTIE said quickly sounds like the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A red from Tuscany in Italy is a well-known wine.

clue.text: Light refreshment in most of France?

definitions.text: Light refreshment in most of France?

indicators.note: in places the light refreshment inside the shortened old name for France
most of means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Gaul is the old Roman name for the land that became France
tea is a light refreshment

explanation.surface: A rich cake served as a snack across most of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims GAUL to GAU, with TEA put in; and the whole clue describes the cake, French for a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich cream cake, its French name, is a refreshment eaten in France, the question mark marking the playful tag.

clue.text: Piece of furniture, jolly old, protected by runner

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed by it, so the marine and old go inside the river

parts.note: a river runs, and the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: An antique cabinet, jolly old, is guarded by an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like 'merry' but is old naval slang for a Royal Marine; 'runner' is a river, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tall cupboard or wardrobe, a French word adopted in English, is a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Feet start to itch Disney character, blowing top

indicators.note: start to takes only the opening letter of itch
blowing one's top means losing the head, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: Bambi is the Disney deer

explanation.surface: A Disney fawn loses its temper as its feet start to itch.
explanation.definitionFit: Metrical units of verse are feet in prosody, and the plural of the unstressed-stressed unit is one kind.

clue.text: Comparatively wet Prince

definitions.meaning: more rainy, the comparative of an adjective for showery weather
Prince of Monaco who married the actress Grace Kelly

explanation.surface: A royal who is rather weaker than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of rainy and the name of Monaco's Prince, husband of Grace Kelly.

clue.text: Home for Derby porcelain originally in some complex

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the jumbled word
complex means intricate or involved, so the letters of some are tangled up
originally points to the beginning, so only the first letter of porcelain is used

explanation.surface: Derby porcelain first turns up in a building complex.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby porcelain is a real china, but here the Derby is the horse race. 'complex' rearranges SOME to ESOM, with P (the first of porcelain) in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby, the famous English flat horse race, is run at the Surrey racecourse of this name, its home.

clue.text: Take off poles surrounding hole in golf range

parts.note: to ape is to mimic, to take off

indicators.note: surrounding means the poles go round the hole number

parts.note: N and S, the north and south poles
the ninth hole, or nine, is a hole on a golf course

explanation.surface: A golfer removes the flagpoles surrounding a hole on the driving range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' is not 'remove' but to mimic; 'range' is a mountain range, not a driving range.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain chain running down the length of Italy is a range of peaks.

clue.text: Unionist chooses to embrace extremists in secret and live elsewhere

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the selected outer letters go inside the word for chooses

parts.note: to pick is to choose

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here those of secret

explanation.surface: A Unionist politician quietly backs extremists and moves away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists in secret' takes S and T, the end letters of 'secret'. To up sticks is a British idiom for moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to pack up and move home, that is, to go and live somewhere else.

clue.text: Extra contains nothing reactionary that identifies reporter

indicators.note: contains means holding the reversed zero inside the cricket extra

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket, scored without the batsman hitting the ball

indicators.note: reactionary means backward-looking, so the word for nothing is read in reverse

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: An extra edition carries nothing reactionary that points to the journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra' seems to be a special edition of a paper but is a cricket bye; 'reactionary' reverses NIL to LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The line at the head of a newspaper article naming the writer identifies the journalist responsible.
